title: STORY TIME: How I broke my ribs squatting
summary: NH tells how he broke his ribs and sprained his intercostal muscles during a 385 lb back squat set after training through spring rib pain, made worse by front squats. The pain kept coming back every spring until he realized his violent pollen-allergy sneezing was re-aggravating the ribs. He fixed it by changing how he sneezes, doing a rib stretch and rehab, and microdosing bee pollen.
claims: Early in his lifting he trained through elbow, lower back and SI joint pain with no injury prevention practice
His rib pain began as a small prick on the left side in spring, worsened and spread to both sides; he kept training through it
Front squats were the worst for the ribs because the front rack stretched them, but he kept doing them for fear of regressing
On a planned 7-rep back squat set at 385 lb he heard a snap at the bottom of the second rep, broke his ribs and sprained the intercostal muscles
The intercostal area has many nerve endings, which makes it extremely painful
He kept training on the broken ribs at first, and in May could barely walk; sneezes were agony
The pain became so linked to squats that just bending his knee triggered it; he was mentally traumatized
He took three months off lower-body work, did upper back work and invented a rib stretch he still does
Rehab timeline: machines for the upper back after one month, dumbbell rows after two, deadlifts with two plates after three
The pain returned every spring; he realized frequent violent sneezing from his pollen allergy was re-aggravating the ribs about 15 times a day
He relearned how to sneeze by just letting the air out; never pinch your nose while sneezing because you can burst an eardrum
He started microdosing bee pollen despite his allergy, and his symptoms faded in 2-3 weeks; he urges care
Ribs heal slowly because they are always moving, and the fear makes rehab hard
He is now at his strongest, lifts lower body pain-free, and still does rib rehab every lower-body day
training_log: planned 7 reps; ribs snapped on rep 2
